title: Psychological and neural responses to architectural interiors
research_questions: Can aesthetic responses to architectural scenes be reduced to a few key psychological dimensions?
Are these dimensions sensitive to salient design features and Global Image Properties (GIPs)?
Do these psychological dimensions correlate with specific patterns of neural activation, and to what extent are these correlations modulated by task?
hypotheses: A few key psychological dimensions would explain much of the variance underlying diverse aesthetic response measures.
These psychological dimensions would be sensitive to ceiling height, enclosure, and curvature.
Each latent psychological dimension would be linked to a distinct pattern of neural activation.

experiment_1.design: Participants rated 200 images of architectural interiors on 16 aesthetic response measures. Each participant rated all images on a subset of 4 measures. Stimuli were counterbalanced for ceiling height (high/low), enclosure (open/closed), and curvature (round/square).
experiment_1.participants: 798 US-based adults (391 women, 401 men, 6 other; M=38.06, SD=11.96 years)
experiment_1.stimuli: 200 images of interior architectural spaces (8 conditions, n=25 per condition)
experiment_1.measures: 16 aesthetic rating scales (Complexity, Organization, Naturalness, Beauty, Personalness, Interest, Modernity, Valence, Stimulation, Vitality, Comfort, Relaxation, Hominess, Uplift, Approachability, Explorability), Self-Similarity (PHOG), Complexity (HOG Complexity)
experiment_1.analysis: Psychometric Network Analysis (PNA), Principal Components Analysis (PCA) with oblimin rotation, 3-way factorial ANOVAs, regression for GIPs

experiment_2.design: Replication study. Participants rated a subset of 16 architectural images on all 9 non-redundant aesthetic rating scales.
experiment_2.participants: 614 American adults (305 women, 307 men, 2 other; M=35.68, SD=10.87 years)
experiment_2.stimuli: Subset of 16 architectural images (1 from each of 16 groups based on 8 architectural conditions + low/high beauty split)
experiment_2.measures: 9 non-redundant aesthetic rating scales (Complexity, Organization, Naturalness, Beauty, Personalness, Interest, Valence, Hominess, Approachability)
experiment_2.analysis: Principal Components Analysis (PCA) with oblimin rotation, 3-way factorial ANOVAs, factor congruence

experiment_3.design: Reanalysis of fMRI data from two previous studies. Participants viewed the same 200 architectural images under two tasks: beauty judgment and approach-avoidance decisions.
experiment_3.participants: 18 healthy participants (12 females, 6 males; M=23.39, SD=4.49 years)
experiment_3.measures: fMRI BOLD signal, Coherence, Fascination, Hominess, Self-similarity, Complexity ratings (from Exp 2 and Exp 1 GIPs)
experiment_3.analysis: Parametric analyses of fMRI data using SPM12, conjunction analysis. Voxel-level p < .001, cluster-level p < .05 FWE.

findings.antecedent: 16 aesthetic response measures for architectural interiors
findings.quote: PNA revealed three communities... PCA identified three components that explained 90% of the variance in ratings.
The first three components... together explained 90% of the variance.
PC1 (Coherence) loaded strongly on Organization (1.04), Beauty (.76), Valence (.74), Approachability (.69).
PC2 (Hominess) loaded strongly on Naturalness (.90), Personalness (.83), Hominess (.73).
PC3 (Fascination) loaded strongly on Complexity (1.02), Interest (.71).
significant main effects of ceiling height [F (1,192) = 13.56, p < .001, ηp² = .08] on PC3 (fascination)
significant main effects of enclosure [F (1,192) = 5.21, p = .024, ηp² = .03] on PC3 (fascination)
significant main effects of ... curvature [F (1,192) = 14.94, p < .001, ηp² = .09] on PC3 (fascination)
significant main effects of enclosure on PC1 [coherence; F (1,192) = 6.39, p = .012, ηp² = .03]
significant main effects of enclosure on PC2 [hominess; F (1,192) = 10.94, p = .001, ηp² = .05]
Self-similarity was found to correlate positively with PC3 (Fascination) scores (r = .242, p < .001)
negatively with PC1 (Coherence) scores (r = -.198, p = .005)
Complexity correlated positively with PC3 (Fascination) scores (r = .519, p < .001)
Complexity correlated positively with PC2 (Hominess) scores (r = .175, p = .013)
The first three components had eigenvalues exceeding Jolliffe's criterion of .7 and together explained 76% of the variance.
PC1 (Hominess) loaded strongly on Naturalness (.90), Personalness (.79), Hominess (.74).
PC2 (Coherence) loaded strongly on Organization (.97), Beauty (.57), Valence (.53), Approachability (.52).
PC3 (Fascination) loaded strongly on Complexity (.98), Interest (.59).
significant main effects of ceiling height [F (1, 9816) = 15.23, p < .001, ηp² = .002] on PC1 (hominess)
significant main effects of enclosure [F (1, 9816) = 118.43, p < .001, ηp² = .012] on PC1 (hominess)
significant main effects of curvature [F (1, 9816) = 20.95, p < .001, ηp² = .002] on PC1 (hominess)
significant main effects of ceiling height [F (1, 9816) = 28.25, p < .001, ηp² = .003] on PC2 (coherence)
significant main effects of enclosure [F (1, 9816) = 180.39, p < .001, ηp² = .018] on PC2 (coherence)
significant main effects of curvature [F (1, 9816) = 13.58, p < .001, ηp² = .001] on PC2 (coherence)
significant main effects were found for ceiling height [F (1, 9816) = 243.00, p < .001, ηp² = .024] on PC3 (fascination)
significant main effects were found for enclosure [F (1, 9816) = 61.21, p < .001, ηp² = .006] on PC3 (fascination)
significant main effects were found for curvature [F (1, 9816) = 232.83, p < .001, ηp² = .023] on PC3 (fascination)

findings.consequent: neural activity in the right lingual gyrus
findings.quote: brain activation encompassing the right lingual gyrus covaried with fascination scores under both beauty judgment and approach-avoidance conditions

findings.consequent: neural activity in the left cuneus
findings.quote: when making approach-avoidance decisions, brain activation encompassing the left cuneus covaried with hominess scores.

findings.consequent: neural activity in the left inferior occipital gyrus
findings.quote: when making beauty judgments, brain activation encompassing the left inferior occipital gyrus covaried with coherence scores

findings.consequent: neural activity in identified visual cortex regions (lingual gyrus, cuneus, inferior occipital gyrus)
findings.quote: brain activation did not covary with self-similarity or complexity scores.

limitations: Used 2D images, limiting generalizability to 3D built spaces.
Focused on visual perception, agnostic about the contribution of nonvisual senses to architectural experiences.
Considered only three basic architectural design variables, which capture a limited proportion of a building's visual properties.
